question: Can this release be published so that the tag, the release notes, the published package and the recorded links all describe the same commit?
trigger: A maintainer wants to cut a release for a git repository that has a version manifest
A recurring release needs the version resolved, tagged, released and published in one command
An existing tag or release must be checked for agreement with the published package
A release must be rehearsed end to end without publishing anything
release-it is already configured and its interfaces must be driven correctly
A half-finished release must be diagnosed before anything else is published
decision: Which version the release carries and how that version was derived
Whether the package, the platform release, or both are published
Whether the run publishes at all, or refuses with nothing published
What the recorded tag, release and package links are
evidence: the repository's version manifest and its git state (branch, clean tree, upstream)
the release-it configuration that resolves for this repository
the tag and the release read back from the platform after publishing
the package version read back from the registry
the recorded links for the tag, the release and the package
success_measure: After one release, the tag, the release notes, the published package and the recorded links all describe the same commit and each is confirmed by reading it back from the platform; otherwise the run refuses and publishes nothing.
outcome: A verified release (tag, release with notes, published package, and links), or a named refusal that published nothing.
intended_users: A maintainer publishing a release of their own repository
An agent asked to cut a release, or to verify one that already ran
input_types: a local git repository with a version manifest (package.json or an equivalent)
a release-it configuration, either existing or scaffolded by the skill
the intended version, or the increment to apply to the current version
output_artifacts: release-plan.json - the resolved version, provider, remote and configuration
release-report.json - the verified tag, release, package and links
use_cases: Cut a release of a repository whose version manifest and git remote are already correct
Work out what the next version would be without publishing anything
Publish and then prove that the tag, the release and the package agree
Read the full interface surface of release-it before writing a configuration

examples.description: Resolve the version, provider and configuration and write release-plan.json without publishing anything.
Publish the release: bump the manifest, commit, tag, create the release with notes and publish the package, then verify all four.
Read the tag, the release and the package back and report whether they describe the same commit.

permissions_systems: Create and push git tags to the configured remote
Create a release with release notes and assets on the hosting platform
Publish a package to the package registry
Read tags, releases and package versions back from the platform
typical_completion_time: 1-3 minutes for a repository that is already configured; a first-time configuration adds a few minutes

data_sources: the platform release API as exposed by the gh command line interface
the platform release API as exposed by the glab command line interface
the package registry as exposed by the npm command line interface
required_capabilities: Node 20 or newer with npm, which release-it runs on
python 3.9 or newer using only the standard library

permissions: Create and push git tags to the configured remote
Create a release with release notes on the hosting platform
Publish a package to the package registry
risk.mutation_scope: The repository's version manifest and changelog, the git history and tags, the platform release, and the published package. Tags, releases and published package versions are public and cannot be withdrawn.
approval_required: A human decides to publish, and does so with the repository checked out, the tree clean and the credentials present
A human accepts that a published version cannot be reused, so a wrong release is corrected by a further release

affected_structures: package.json (or the repository's equivalent version manifest)
git commits, git tags and the configured remote
the platform release and its notes
invariants: The version in the manifest always equals the tag name with its prefix removed
The release is created from the commit the tag resolves to, never from the branch head
A version that has been published is never published again
The recorded links name the same version as the manifest, the tag and the release
sources_of_truth: the released version: the version field of the repository's manifest read after the bump
the released commit: git rev-list -n 1 <tag>, which dereferences the annotated tag to a commit
the tag that exists on the remote: git ls-remote --tags origin <tag> including its peeled line
the published package version: npm view <package>@<version> version
the created release: the platform release read back by tag name
invalid_states_prevented: a tag exists but the package was never published
the package was published but no tag exists
the release notes name a different version from the tag
the tag points at a commit that is not the commit the artifact was built from
a release was created from the branch head because the named tag did not exist yet
state_transitions: clean -> version resolved -> manifest bumped -> committed -> tagged -> release created -> package published -> verified
failure before the tag lands -> nothing published -> clean
failure after the tag lands -> tagged but unreleased -> a further release corrects it

identifiers: the repository owner and name, derived from the git remote
the tag name, which is the version with the configured prefix
the version string, which the manifest and the package registry share
relationships: One version yields exactly one tag and at most one release
One release belongs to exactly one tag, and that tag resolves to exactly one commit
One published package version belongs to exactly one released version
field_semantics: a tag name is the manifest version carrying the configured prefix
release notes describe the changes between the previous tag and this tag
whether a release is a draft or a prerelease is a platform property, not a version property
invariants: A release is only ever reported as verified when its tag, its notes, its package and its links all name the same version
Reading back is what establishes the release; a successful exit code alone does not
freshness_and_pagination: Read-back happens after the publish step, so the record is as fresh as the run
Listing tags or releases is paged, so a lookup by exact tag name is used rather than a scan of the first page
nullability: A repository legitimately has no releases yet, and no previous tag for the first release
A repository may publish no package at all, in which case the package check reports absent rather than failing
readiness_checks: the release command line interface is present and authenticated
the tag lookup by exact name returns either the expected record or a definite absence

required_operations: read a tag by exact name and resolve it to a commit
read a release by tag name including its notes
read a published package version back from the registry
create a release with release notes for an existing tag
semantic_recon.freshness_check: the release interface is probed live before it is trusted, and a report that is not fresh and usable is a safe stop rather than a licence to publish
